translationRepairs: Junli followed the campaigns against Keju's army and won victory after victory. When the Ancestor of Offerings fled into the Tatar lands, Junli held the Ganyi army. The Martial Emperor received the Yanmen command, made Junli his left chief guard officer, marched with him through the passes, drove off Huang Chao's remnant forces, and recovered Chang'an.

Junli followed the campaigns against Keju's army and won victory after victory. When the Ancestor of Offerings fled into the Tatar lands, Junli held the Ganyi army. The Martial Emperor received the Yanmen command, made Junli his left chief guard officer, marched with him through the passes, drove off Huang Chao, and recovered Chang'an.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 黃孽 is an epithet for Huang Chao himself, not specifically remnant forces; the campaign recovered Chang'an from Huang Chao.
When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Junli as Grand Tutor in remembrance of old service.
When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he posthumously honored Junli as Grand Tutor in remembrance of old service.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 詔贈太傅 is a posthumous honorary appointment, not an enfeoffment.
he followed into the Tatar lands; when the Martial Emperor received the Yanmen command, Zhiqin led the north-of-Dai army commissioner;
he followed into the Tatar lands; when the Martial Emperor received the Yanmen command, Zhiqin became commissioner of the armies north of Dai;
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 領代北軍使 means he held the office of Dai-north army commissioner, not that he led a commissioner.

Zhiqin's fierce courage was unmatched; moreover, wine had stirred his boldness. He alone climbed the post-station tower and shouted, "Vice Director Zhu has betrayed kindness and acted without honor, luring our Minister to plot against him—my three hundred men are enough to settle the affair!"

Zhiqin's fierce courage was unmatched; moreover, wine had stirred his boldness. He alone climbed the post-station tower and shouted, "Vice Director Zhu has betrayed kindness and acted without honor, luring our Minister in order to plot against him—my three hundred men are enough to settle the affair!"

Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 邀我司空圖之 is 司空 plus 圖之 (plot against him), not the personal name 司空圖; the literal 'to plot against him' attached to the Minister reverses the agent.
With Li Sizhao he attacked Fenzhou, was first over the wall, captured the rebel general Li Tang and presented him to command, and was appointed acting Minister of Works.
With Li Sizhao he attacked Fenzhou, was first over the wall, captured the rebel general Li Tang and presented him, and was appointed acting Minister of Works.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 以獻 means he presented the captive; 'to command' is not in the Chinese.
The Bian general Shi Yanzhang repeatedly raided southern Zhao. Jiantang ambushed him at Baixiang, captured him, and presented him to command.
The Bian general Shi Yanzhang repeatedly raided southern Zhao. Jiantang ambushed him at Baixiang, captured him, and presented him.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 獻之 means he presented the captive; 'to command' is not in the Chinese.
When the imperial army attacked Huayin, Huang Chao sent the false director of the guest bureau Wang Ting to confer on strategy with Huang Kui. Chengsi captured him and presented him to command.
When the imperial army attacked Huayin, Huang Chao sent the false director of the guest bureau Wang Ting to confer on strategy with Huang Kui. Chengsi captured him and presented him.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 以獻 means presented the captive; 'to command' is not in the Chinese.
During Zhu Mei's rebellion Chengsi led ten thousand men to relieve Binzhou and met the imperial carriage at the Wei Bridge to escort it.
During Zhu Mei's rebellion Chengsi led ten thousand men to relieve Fuzhou and met the imperial carriage at the Wei Bridge to escort it.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 鄜州 is Fuzhou, not Binzhou (邠州).
When the Martial Emperor rose in Yunzhong, Yu with Kang Junli and others pushed the wheel and aided him, and thereby became his trusted core.
When the Martial Emperor rose in Yunzhong, Yu with Kang Junli and others supported and aided him, and thereby became his trusted core.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 推轂佐佑 is a metaphor for supporting a rise; 'pushed the wheel' is unnaturally literal and obscures the meaning.
When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne he posthumously enfeoffed Yu as Grand Preceptor.
When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne he posthumously honored Yu as Grand Preceptor.
Independent review confirms the correction against the chapter text. 追贈太師 is a posthumous honorary appointment, not an enfeoffment.
